stem: The student wants to present the aim of Ferrer's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• At the site of Tambo Viejo in Peru, archaeologists uncovered dozens of circular stone storage buildings.
• Researchers had long disagreed about whether the buildings once held grain or dried meat.
• In 2022, archaeologist Lucía Ferrer led a team that sought to determine what had been stored in the buildings.
• The team analyzed chemical residues preserved in the buildings' clay floors.
• They detected traces of maize starch in nearly every building.
choices: Ferrer's team detected traces of maize starch in nearly every one of the circular stone buildings at Tambo Viejo.
Ferrer's 2022 study sought to determine what had been stored in the circular stone buildings at Tambo Viejo.
Ferrer's team analyzed chemical residues preserved in the clay floors of the stone buildings at Tambo Viejo.
Researchers had long disagreed about whether the stone buildings at Tambo Viejo held grain or dried meat.
explanation: The goal asks for the aim, meaning the purpose or question behind the study. Choice B uses the note saying Ferrer's team "sought to determine what had been stored in the buildings," so it states exactly what the study set out to learn.

A.why: You picked the study's finding. That is the result, not the aim. The goal asked what the team wanted to find out, not what it discovered.

C.why: You picked the method. Analyzing floor residues is how the team did the study, not why it did it.

D.why: You picked the background. This is the disagreement that came before the study, and it never mentions Ferrer's study or what it set out to do.

stem: The student wants to present the conclusion of Okafor's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Small earthquakes sometimes occur in tight clusters called swarms.
• Seismologist Daniel Okafor investigated whether swarms beneath Haldane Ridge were caused by moving underground fluids.
• His team placed 40 seismometers across the ridge and monitored them for 18 months.
• The instruments recorded more than 6,000 small earthquakes.
• The team concluded that the swarms were triggered by water migrating upward through cracks in the rock.
choices: Okafor's team placed 40 seismometers across Haldane Ridge and monitored them for a period of 18 months.
Okafor investigated whether earthquake swarms beneath Haldane Ridge were caused by moving underground fluids.
Over 18 months, seismometers on Haldane Ridge recorded more than 6,000 small earthquakes in swarms.
Okafor's team concluded that the swarms beneath Haldane Ridge were triggered by water rising through cracks in rock.
explanation: The goal asks for the conclusion, so you need the stage where the researchers say what their results mean. Choice D uses the "concluded" note: water moving upward through cracks set off the swarms.

A.why: You picked the method. Placing and monitoring seismometers describes how the study was done, not what the team concluded.

B.why: You picked the aim. This is the question Okafor asked, not the answer the team reached.

C.why: You picked the raw data. A count of recorded earthquakes is an observation. It doesn't say what caused the swarms, and that is what the conclusion explains.

stem: The student wants to present Lindqvist's study and its findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Portolan charts were nautical maps drawn in the Mediterranean region between the 1300s and 1600s.
• Historian Mira Lindqvist wanted to know how accurately the charts depicted coastlines.
• She compared the coastlines on 25 portolan charts with modern satellite maps.
• She found that distances along the charts' coastlines differed from actual distances by an average of only 5 percent.
choices: Lindqvist compared the coastlines drawn on 25 portolan charts with those shown on modern satellite maps.
Comparing 25 portolan charts with satellite maps, Lindqvist found their coastline distances were off by only 5 percent.
Lindqvist wanted to know how accurately portolan charts, drawn between the 1300s and 1600s, depicted coastlines.
Coastline distances on portolan charts differ from actual distances by an average of only about 5 percent.
explanation: "Study and its findings" needs two things: what Lindqvist did and what she found. Choice B names the study (comparing 25 charts with satellite maps) and the result (an average error of only 5 percent).

A.why: You picked a choice that gives only the study's method and never reports what Lindqvist found. The goal asks for both.

C.why: You picked the aim. It states Lindqvist's question but not her study's method or result.

D.why: You picked a choice that gives only the finding. It never mentions Lindqvist or her study, so the reader can't tell where the 5 percent figure came from.
